(PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE N.S.SANJAY GOWDA)
1.
The claimants are in appeal challenging the dismissal of the claim petitions.

The claimants in MFA.No.200414/2018 filed a claim petition seeking for compensation for the Jayashree vs Shivanand And Anr on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135393768/
3 death of Shivalingappa, 52 years old.

It was stated that Shivalingappa was traveling in a Omni car and the driver had stopped the said car to attend a nature call and he had parked the vehicle negligently and since it was night time, the said car was not spotted by the driver of a lorry who collided with the lorry and as a result of this impact, Shivalingappa sustained serious injuries and died at the spot.
It was asserted that the accident occurred only because of the fault on the part of the driver of the Omni car.

3. The Tribunal has recorded a finding that there was negligence on the part of the driver of the omni car and since the lorry which hit the omni car, was not traced and a 'C' report was filed by the police, the insurer of the Omni car would not be responsible for the accident and it has proceeded to dismiss the petition.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:6868 4.
At the outset, it is to be stated here that the Omni car was insured with a package policy.
By virtue of the issuance of a package policy, it cannot be in dispute that the occupants of the car would stand automatically covered.

It is also noticed that, apart from the automatic coverage of all the occupants under the package policy, the Insurer also collected an additional personal accident cover premium for a sum of `1,00,000/- per person, for a total of eight persons, amounting to `400/-.

In the light of the fact that the Insurer had issued a comprehensive package policy and had also given a cover of personal accident to eight unnamed passengers as an additional cover, it cannot be argued that the Insurer can be absolved of all liability because, there was negligence on the part of the driver of the omni car.
5. Whenever a vehicle is covered under comprehensive policy, the negligence on the part of the driver would not really be relevant.

All that would be required is for an accident to occur to the car and if as a NC: 2024:KHC-K:6868 result of the accident, the occupants are hurt or killed, the liability of the Insurer would automatically be attracted.

6. In the light of this, the finding of the Tribunal that the driver of the omni car was negligent in parking the car on the road, which caused the accident and hence the Insurer cannot be made liable cannot be accepted and the finding is therefore set aside.
7. As far as compensation is concerned, the deceased was aged about 52 years and doing agriculture work.
There is however no acceptable evidence regarding his monthly income.
In such cases, the sum of `7,000/- determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority will have to be applied which for the year 2013.

8. As per the decision of the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs.
Pranay Sethi and Others1, as the deceased was aged about 52 years, 10% of the same (`700/-) is required to (2017) 16 SCC 680 NC: 2024:KHC-K:6868 be added to the said income as future prospects and the resultant income would thus be `7,700/-.

Out of the said sum, 1/4th of the same (`1,925/-) would have to be deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased, as he was survived by his wife and three children.

The net income will be `5,775/-.
10.

As the deceased was aged 52 years, as per the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another2, a multiplier of '11' would have to be applied.

sentences.text: Consequently, towards 'loss of dependency', a sum of `7,62,300/- is awarded (`5,775/-x 12 x 11).

11. The claimants being the widow and children, each of them would be entitled to a sum of `48,400/- towards loss of love and affection i.e., in all `1,93,600/- (2009) 6 SCC 121 NC:
2024:KHC-K:6868 and a further sum of `36,300/- will have to be awarded under the conventional heads.

12. Thus, the claimants would be entitled to the following sums :
 Sl. Compensation as  Nature of Heads  No. awarded by this Court (`)
 1. Loss of Dependency 7,62,300/-
 2. Loss of love and affection 1,93,600/-
 3. Conventional heads 36,300/-
 Total 9,92,200/-
13.

Thus, the claimants in MFA No.200413/2018 would be entitled for compensation of `9,92,200/-
along with interest at the rate of six per cent per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

14. As far as the other claimant - Jayashree in MFA No.200414/2018 is concerned, the wound certificate Ex.P.3 only indicates that she had a swelling of the right wrist and a contusion on her right chest.
It is indicated that she was hospitalized for two days.

The treated Doctor NC:
2024:KHC-K:6868 has however not been examined.
In my view, having regard to the wound certificate, it would be appropriate to award a sum of `25,000/- as a global compensation for injuries suffered by her.
15. Consequently, the appeals are allowed in part to the above said extent.
16. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded along with interest within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

5 17.

On such deposit being made, out of the compensation awarded to appellants, 25% of the award amount shall be invested in any nationalized bank or post office deposit for an initial period of five years.
They shall, however, be entitled to draw periodical interest on the said amount.
The remaining sum shall be disbursed to them in equal proportions on proper identification.
In MFA No.200414/2018, the entire award amount along with interest shall be disbursed to the claimant forthwith.
